key_insight: Co-optimizing network topology, dynamic line ratings, and variable impedance devices can reduce grid congestion and operating costs while iterative McCormick relaxation improves solution accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports coordinated use of grid-enhancing technologies to better utilize existing power transmission infrastructure.
method: Model topology switching with a node-breaker formulation.
Adjust transmission limits using weather-dependent dynamic line ratings.
Iteratively refine McCormick relaxations of bilinear impedance terms.
evidence_signal: IEEE 118-bus tests and additional benchmark studies report improved accuracy over standard McCormick relaxation, solution quality close to the nonlinear formulation, and computational efficiency.
watch_item: Relaxed solutions require feasibility checks against the original nonlinear constraints; the abstract provides no numerical accuracy or runtime results.
paper_title: Co-Optimization of Network Topology and Variable Impedance Devices under Dynamic Line Ratings Using Iterative McCormick Relaxation
